lamina.name: Metabolic
lamina.description: Tissue oxygen metabolism: what the supply allows, what the demand asks for, and the lactate that measures the gap. The receiving end of the first channel in this body with a return path.

attribute.name: Oxygen Supply Index
attribute.description: The composite STATE VALUE respiration presents at its face, and the only thing this lamina learns about the world below it. An INDEX in [0,1], NOT oxygen delivery in mL/min: the face it comes from blends four attributes into one number, so naming it DO2 would claim a precision the wire does not carry — measured, the same index would read as 1715.8 mL/min against a true 988. Until a gate opens onto it, it rests at the baseline below and the snapshot says "baseline (uncoupled)" rather than letting a placeholder pass for a live coupled value. No noise_sigma: a synthetic feed does not emit for this source, and jitter here would be inventing a measurement error for a number that is not a measurement.

attribute.name: Oxygen Demand
attribute.description: How much oxygen the tissue is asking for this cycle. Roughly 250 mL/min at rest for an adult; exercise raises it several-fold, and driving this attribute is how a test makes the supply seam matter. It is a SENSOR because metabolic demand is set outside this model — by activity, temperature, and work — not derived from anything inside it.

attribute.name: Oxygen Consumption Capacity
attribute.description: What this tissue could consume if the supply index were 1.0 — the scale that turns a dimensionless index into mL/min. It belongs here rather than on the sending lamina because it is a property of the consumer: the same oxygen supply means something different to a resting calf and to a working myocardium.

attribute.name: Baseline Lactate
attribute.description: Resting arterial lactate with no oxygen deficit at all. Normal is under 2 mmol/L, and about 1.0 in a well-perfused adult.

attribute.name: Lactate Yield
attribute.description: How much lactate a sustained oxygen deficit produces. Declared here rather than written into the Python, following the lesson CVP taught this project: a coefficient buried in code is one a domain expert can neither see nor change. At the baseline of 0.015 a deficit of 200 mL/min lifts lactate from 1.0 to 4.0 — comfortably out of the target band, which is what makes the supply seam observable.

attribute.name: Oxygen Consumption
attribute.description: What the tissue actually consumes: its demand, or the ceiling the arriving supply allows, whichever is smaller. The min() IS the elbow — above the critical supply this equals demand and does not care what the lung is doing, below it consumption follows supply down.

attribute.name: Supply Utilisation
attribute.description: What fraction of the CONSUMABLE oxygen this tissue is using — VO2 over the ceiling, so it reaches exactly 1.0 when consumption becomes supply-limited. Deliberately NOT called the oxygen extraction ratio: a true O2ER is VO2 over oxygen DELIVERED, and this lamina never receives a delivery in mL/min, only an index. Naming it O2ER would put a familiar clinical label on a different quantity, which is the mistake Q carries in the circulatory lamina and which this project has spent real effort undoing. Reported rather than acted on: it says HOW CLOSE the tissue is to the elbow, which a lactate of exactly baseline does not.

attribute.name: Oxygen Deficit
attribute.description: The shortfall between what was asked for and what was consumed, and the only quantity here that is zero when everything is fine. Floored at zero: a tissue offered more than it asked for has no surplus to bank, because consumption is already capped at demand upstream.

attribute.name: Arterial Lactate
attribute.description: The endpoint of this lamina and the outcome the return path carries. A deliberately linear stand-in for anaerobic metabolism — no clearance, no time constant, no acid-base coupling — which gets right the one thing this body needs from it: it sits at baseline while supply meets demand, and rises when it does not, for a reason no correction inside THIS lamina could fix.

function.name: Oxygen Consumption
function.description: The biphasic DO2/VO2 relationship in one line (Cain 1977). supply_index * VO2_capacity is the ceiling — the most this tissue could consume given what arrived. Below the ceiling, consumption is set by demand and is independent of supply, which is why a healthy person does not consume more oxygen by breathing harder.

function.name: Supply Utilisation
function.description: The denominator is the same ceiling as step 1, recomputed rather than passed along, so the two can never disagree about what was on offer. A ceiling of zero or less is refused rather than divided by — a utilisation fraction of infinity is not a measurement.

function.name: Oxygen Deficit
function.description: What the tissue asked for and did not get. Zero whenever consumption met demand, which is the ordinary case.

function.name: Lactate Production
function.description: Anaerobic metabolism as a straight line through the deficit. Both coefficients are declared attributes rather than constants in Python, so the relation can be retuned without touching code.

composite.name: Tissue State
composite.description: How the tissue is faring: what arrived, what it used, how much of the available supply it is using, and what that cost.

segment.name: Tissue Oxygenation
segment.description: Supply, demand, and the gap between them
segment.attributes: supply_index, VO2_demand, VO2_capacity, lactate_base, lactate_k, VO2, O2_utilisation, O2_deficit, lactate

outcome.name: Target Lactate
outcome.description: Normal arterial lactate is under 2 mmol/L; the band here is 0 to 2. This is the outcome whose error travels BACK up the supply channel, because it is the one this lamina cannot act on: a tissue has no pump and no lung. Everything that could raise oxygen supply lives one lamina down.
